Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,re,json
from collections import Counter
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
for name,ik,ok in [('d1','Demo pair 1 input','Demo pair 1 output'),('d2','Demo pair 2 input','Demo pair 2 output')]:
    I,O=G[ik],G[ok]; h,w=len(I),len(I[0]); bg=Counter(x for row in I for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    new=[(r,c,O[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if O[r][c]!=bg and I[r][c]==bg]
    print(name,'bg',bg); print(' pts',pts)
    print(' new',new)

def solve2(I):
    h,w=len(I),len(I[0]); bg=Counter(x for row in I for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    O=[row[:] for row in I]
    def paint(r,c,val):
        if 0<=r<h and 0<=c<w and I[r][c]==bg: O[r][c]=val
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            v=I[r][c]
            if v==bg: continue
            # main diagonal dir (+1,+1)
            rr,cc=r+1,c+1
            while rr<h and cc<w and I[rr][cc]==bg: paint(rr,cc,v); rr+=1; cc+=1
            rr,cc=r-1,c-1
            while rr>=0 and cc>=0 and I[rr][cc]==bg: paint(rr,cc,v); rr-=1; cc-=1
            rr,cc=r+1,c-1
            while rr<h and cc>=0 and I[rr][cc]==bg: paint(rr,cc,v); rr+=1; cc-=1
            rr,cc=r-1,c+1
            while rr>=0 and cc<w and I[rr][cc]==bg: paint(rr,cc,v); rr-=1; cc+=1
    return O

from collections import defaultdict
def f(I):
    h,w=len(I),len(I[0])
    bg=Counter(x for row in I for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    O=[row[:] for row in I]
    def put(r,c,col):
        if 0<=r<h and 0<=c<w and O[r][c]==bg: O[r][c]=col
    mks=[(r,c,I[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if I[r][c]!=bg]
    gM=defaultdict(list); gA=defaultdict(list)
    for r,c,v in mks:
        gM[r-c].append((r,c,v)); gA[r+c].append((r,c,v))
    # main-diag lines (r-c const, slope +1 going down-right): fill between extremes same color; interior markers -> full perpendicular anti-diagonals
    for dk,p in sorted(gM.items()):
        p=sorted(p,key=lambda q:(q[0],q[1]))
        if len(p)<2: continue
        k=0
        while k<len(p)-1:
            j=k
            while j+1<len(p) and p[j][2]==p[j+1][2]: j+=1
            colv=p[k][2]
            for rr in range(min(p[k][0],p[j][0])+1,max(p[k][0],p[j][0])):
                cc=rr-dk
                if 0<=cc<w and O[rr][cc]==bg: O[rr][cc]=colv
            for m in p[k:j+1]:
                for rr in range(h):
                    cc=m[0]+dk-m[0]  # placeholder
            k=j+1
    return O
for n in [5]:
    I=G['Demo pair %d input'%n]; O_=G['Demo pair %d output'%n]
    print(n, f(I)==O_)

from collections import defaultdict, Counter
for n in range(1,6):
    I,O=G['Demo pair %d input'%n],G['Demo pair %d output'%n]
    h,w=len(I),len(I[0])
    bg=Counter(x for row in I for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    mks=[(r,c,I[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if I[r][c]!=bg]
    print('=== demo',n,'markers',mks)
    lines=defaultdict(list); anti=defaultdict(list)
    for r,c,v in mks:
        lines[r-c].append((r,c,v)); anti[r+c].append((r,c,v))
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if I[r][c]==bg and O[r][c]!=bg:
                line=(r-c,r+c,O[r][c])
                onmain=[p for p in lines[line[0]]]
                onanti=[p for p in anti[line[1]]]
                print(f'  ({r},{c})->{line} main:{onmain} anti:{onanti}')

```python
def f(I):
    h,w=len(I),len(I[0])
    bg=Counter(x for row in I for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    O=[row[:] for row in I]
    def put(r,c,col):
        if 0<=r<h and 0<=c<w and O[r][c]==bg: O[r][c]=col
    # collect markers
    mks=[(r,c,I[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if I[r][c]!=bg]
    # diagonals per marker: main d=r-c, anti s=r+c
    byd=defaultdict(list); bes=defaultdict(list)
    for r,c,v in mks:
        byd[r-c].append((r,c,v)); bes[r+c].append((r,c,v))
    for dk,ps in byd.items():
        ps.sort()
        # group consecutive same-color runs
        k=0
        while k<len(ps):
            j=k
            while j+1<len(ps) and ps[j][2]==ps[j+1][2]: j+=1
            colv=ps[k][2]; others={p[2] for p in ps if p[2]!=colv}
            # fill between extremes of this run
            for rr in range(min(ps[k][0],ps[j][0])+1,max(ps[k][0],ps[j][0])):
                cc=rr-dk
                if 0<=cc<w and O[rr][cc]==bg: O[rr][cc]=colv
            # emission: if color!=bg and len(others)==1 and that color != colv? 
            # condition: diagonal has markers of >=2 distinct colors? or others set size==1
            if len(others)>0 and len({p[2] for p in ps})>1:
                emit = colv==6  # 6 emits
                if emit:
                    s=dk+ps[k][0]-ps[k][0]+... 
                    # perpendicular anti-diagonal through emitter: s = r+c through emitter position (r,c)
                    pass
            k=j+1
    return O
```
